Q705111.label: Joseph Pholien
aliases: Joseph Clovis Louis Marie Emmanuel Pholien
Q705111.img: Brussels, Palais de la Nation, Joseph Pholien.jpg
Q705111.summary: Joseph Clovis Louis Marie Emmanuel Pholien was a Belgian Catholic politician and member of the PSC-CVP. He was born in Liège, and volunteered to serve with the Belgian army during World War I, being commissioned as a first lieutenant. He was the minister of Justice under Paul-Henri Spaak from May 1938 to February 1939 and was the prime minister of Belgium from 16 August 1950 to 15 January 1952. In 1966, he became a minister of State.
tags: Position held:Minister of Justice of Belgium

Q211543.label: 1985 Belgian general election
Q211543.summary: General elections were held in Belgium on 13 October 1985. The Christian People's Party emerged as the largest party, with 49 of the 212 seats in the Chamber of Representatives and 25 of the 106 seats in the Senate. Elections to the nine provincial councils were also held.

Q1801303.label: 2007 Belgian federal election
Q1801303.summary: Federal elections were held in Belgium on 10 June 2007. Voters went to the polls in order to elect new members for the Chamber of Representatives and Senate.

Q276567.label: Zhelyu Zhelev
Q276567.summary: Zhelyu Mitev Zhelev was a Bulgarian politician and former dissident who served as the first democratically elected and non-Communist president of Bulgaria, from 1990 to 1997. Zhelev was one of the most prominent figures of the 1989 Bulgarian Revolution, which ended the 35 year rule of President Todor Zhivkov. A member of the Union of Democratic Forces, he was elected as president by the 7th Grand National Assembly. Two years later, he won Bulgaria's first direct presidential elections.

Positions held: member of the Bulgarian National Assembly

tags: Position held:Member of the Bulgarian National Assembly

Q421463.label: Bulgarian nuclear power referendum
Q421463.summary: A referendum on building a new nuclear power plant was held in Bulgaria on 27 January 2013. Whilst it was not explicitly mentioned in the question, it was widely acknowledged that the referendum was about restarting construction at the Belene Nuclear Power Plant.

Q62551.label: Mikhail Kasianov
Q62551.desc: Russian politician, Prime Minister of Russia (2000–2004)
Q62551.summary: Mikhail Mikhailovich Kasyanov is a Russian politician who served as Prime Minister of Russia from 2000 to 2004. Previously, he had served as First Deputy Prime Minister in 2000 and Minister of Finance from 1999 to 2000. During the 1990s, he worked in President Boris Yeltsin's administration in different positions before joining President Vladimir Putin's first administration. He has the federal state civilian service rank of 1st class Active State Councillor of the Russian Federation.

Positions held: First Deputy Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation

mentions.c: Head of government of Soviet Union / Russia, 2000–2004

tags: Position held:First Deputy Chairman of the Government of the Russian Federation

Q7035479.label: Nikol Pashinyan
Q7035479.summary: Nikol Vovayi Pashinyan is an Armenian politician who has served as the 16th and current prime minister of Armenia since 2018. A journalist by profession, Pashinyan founded his own newspaper in 1998, which was shut down a year later for libel. He was sentenced for one year for defamation against then Minister of National Security Serzh Sargsyan.

Positions held: member of the National Assembly of Armenia

tags: Position held:Member of the National Assembly of Armenia

Q56400471.label: 2024 Finnish presidential election
aliases: Election of the President of the Republic 2024
Q56400471.summary: Presidential elections were held in Finland on 28 January 2024, with a second round held on 11 February. Voters elected a president of the Republic for a six-year term.

Q18332247.label: 2018 Swedish general election
Q18332247.summary: General elections were held in Sweden on 9 September 2018 to elect the 349 members of the Riksdag. Regional and municipal elections were also held on the same day.

Q60042839.label: 2018 Sunda Strait tsunami
Q60042839.desc: tsunami in coastal regions of Banten and Lampung, Indonesia
Q60042839.summary: The 2018 Sunda Strait tsunami occurred on 22 December 2018 at around 21:38 local time after large parts of the southwestern side of Anak Krakatoa collapsed onto its caldera. The landslide spawned a tsunami wave that struck multiple coastal regions in Banten and Lampung, including the tourist destination of Anyer.

mentions.c: Indonesia: Natural disaster: 2018 Sunda Strait tsunami

Q16471.label: Invasion of Normandy
Q16471.desc: 1944 invasion and establishment of Western Allied forces in Normandy during WWII
Q16471.img: Into the Jaws of Death 23-0455M edit.jpg
Q16471.summary: Operation Overlord was the codename for the Battle of Normandy, the Allied operation that launched the successful invasion of German-occupied Western Europe during World War II. The operation was launched on 6 June 1944 (D-Day) with the Normandy landings. A 1,200-plane airborne assault preceded an amphibious assault involving more than 5,000 vessels. Nearly 160,000 troops crossed the English Channel on 6 June, and more than two million Allied troops were in France by the end of August.

Q1678423.label: Battle of FSB Mary Ann
Q1678423.summary: The Battle of FSB Mary Ann occurred when Viet Cong (VC) sappers attacked a U.S. firebase located in Quảng Tín Province, South Vietnam early on the morning of 28 March 1971.

Q1760855.label: Battle of Đồng Hới
Q1760855.summary: The Battle of Đồng Hới was a clash between United States Navy (USN) warships and Vietnam People's Air Force (VPAF) MiG-17F fighter bombers and shore batteries on 19 April 1972, during the Vietnam War. This was the second time U.S. warships faced an air attack since the end of World War II, excluding the USS Liberty incident, which was officially recorded as an attack by mistake.

Q7096919.label: Operation Commando Fury
Q7096919.desc: Afghan military operation against the Taliban
Q7096919.img: Afghan commandos during Operation Commando Fury.jpg
Q7096919.summary: Operation Commando Fury was a four-day Afghan military operation against the Taliban in the Kapisa Province. Six insurgents were killed and six others were captured.

Q21190743.label: 2015 Kuweires offensive
Q21190743.summary: On 14 September 2015, the Syrian Arab Army (SAA) – in cooperation with the National Defence Forces (NDF) and the Al-Ba'ath Battalion – launched a fresh offensive inside the Aleppo Governorate's southeastern countryside in order to lift the Islamic State's (ISIS) two-year-long siege of the isolated Kuweires Military Airbase. This offensive was later complemented by another effort starting mid-October further south, which would be aimed at cementing government control over the main logistical route to Aleppo from central Syria.

Q112163927.label: Northern Ukraine border skirmishes
Q112163927.desc: border skirmishes in the Russian invasion of Ukraine
Q112163927.summary: A series of border skirmishes has taken place along the Russia–Ukraine border in Sumy and Chernihiv Oblasts since the withdrawal of Russian troops from northern Ukraine. Ukrainian officials have stated that strikes across the border happen daily.

mentions.c: Part of Russian invasion of Ukraine

Q125870679.label: 2024 northern Kharkiv offensive
Q125870679.desc: battle in the Russian invasion of Ukraine in 2024
Q125870679.summary: On 10 May 2024, the Russian Armed Forces began an offensive operation in Ukraine's Kharkiv Oblast, shelling and attempting to breach the defenses of the Ukrainian Armed Forces in the direction of Vovchansk and Kharkiv. The Guardian reported that the offensive led to Russia's biggest territorial gains in 18 months. By early June the Russian offensive stalled, with The Guardian reporting that the situation on the frontline had been "stabilized." Ukrainian forces then began small-scale counterattacks, which reportedly recaptured a settlement on 19 June.

mentions.c: Part of Russian invasion of Ukraine

Q126370903.label: Wad An Nora massacre
Q126370903.summary: The Wad Al-Noora massacre started at around 05:00 (GMT+2) on 5 June 2024, when the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) attacked the village of Wad Al-Noora in Al-Jazira state twice, killing at least 100 civilians. The massacre followed after the RSF besieging and opening fire on the village.

mentions.c: Part of Sudanese civil war (2023–present); 200 deaths
